summary_alerts.html:
CONSENSUS BUY — GOOGL (Capito (R) + Fetterman (D) + Taylor (R) + Keating (D), cross-party)
4 members, combined disclosed value ~$32K. Four members spanning both parties—Capito (R), Fetterman (D), Taylor (R), and Keating (D)—independently accumulated Alphabet (GOOGL) positions during the window, representing the broadest cross-aisle consensus buy in the cohort. Bipartisan convergence of this magnitude on a single large-cap technology name is statistically uncommon and elevates the signal quality above routine portfolio overlap.

CONSENSUS BUY — HD (Khanna (D) + McCormick (R) + Taylor (R), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$99K. Home Depot (HD) attracted cross-party accumulation from Khanna (D), McCormick (R), and Taylor (R), with a combined disclosed buy volume of approximately $99K. Concurrent positioning by members with divergent ideological profiles suggests shared confidence in housing-adjacent consumer spending and home-improvement demand, potentially ahead of a seasonal upturn or in anticipation of infrastructure-linked tail winds.

CONSENSUS BUY — MSFT (Fetterman (D) + Taylor (R) + McCormick (R), cross-party)
3 members, combined disclosed value ~$48K. Microsoft (MSFT) was purchased independently by Fetterman (D), Taylor (R), and McCormick (R), underscoring continued institutional confidence in enterprise cloud and AI infrastructure among members with access to relevant policy discussions. The three-member signal places MSFT among the highest-conviction cross-party buys in the 60-day window.

CONSENSUS SELL — AAPL (Suozzi (D) + Taylor (R), cross-party)
2 members, combined disclosed value ~$40K. Rohit Khanna (D) and Richard McCormick (R) each disclosed purchases of both Abbott Laboratories (ABT) and BlackRock (BLK) during the window, producing a paired cross-party signal in healthcare devices and asset management. The coincidence of both members accumulating the same two names—one defensive-yield healthcare name and one financial-sector titan—may reflect a rotation toward dividend-paying, inflation-resilient holdings.

CONSENSUS SELL — T (Fetterman (D) + Taylor (R), cross-party)
2 members, combined disclosed value ~$16K. Apple (AAPL) saw cross-party selling from Suozzi (D) and Taylor (R), both disclosing disposals during the same window. Concurrent reductions across party lines in the most widely held U.S. equity may signal profit-taking following an extended valuation premium, wariness around potential antitrust or tariff exposure, or portfolio rebalancing ahead of a perceived near-term risk.

CONSENSUS SELL — WAT (Dingell (D) + Hern (R), cross-party)
2 members, combined disclosed value ~$16K. Kevin Hern (R-OK) disclosed 15 sell transactions and zero purchases across the 60-day window, representing the most concentrated single-member bearish posture in the cohort. The absence of any offsetting buy activity over a two-month period distinguishes Hern's positioning from routine rebalancing and warrants attention as a potential leading indicator of sector-level concern from a member with relevant committee exposure.

CONVICTION — Kevin Hern TXN ~$750K
Rohit Khanna (D-CA) recorded 67 disclosed buy transactions totaling approximately $1.34M in buy volume—the highest in the cohort by a substantial margin—against only 8 sells, yielding a strongly bullish designation. Given Khanna's committee assignments and publicly stated technology policy positions, the sustained pace and scale of accumulation reflect a high-conviction outlook toward the technology and innovation sectors over the period.
